Since implementing Freshservice, our onboarding and offboarding workflows have become far more efficient and transparent. For onboarding, we now use standardized ticket templates and automated approval chains, which has reduced our average “time to provision” from 5 days down to 2 days—a 60% improvement. New-hire satisfaction scores have climbed by roughly 15 points (on a 100-point scale), largely because employees receive all their required access and equipment on day one with minimal manual follow-up.

On the offboarding side, scripted workflows automatically revoke access, archive mailboxes, and update asset inventories. As a result, our offboarding time has dropped from an average of 3 days to under 24 hours, and our offboarding task-completion rate has remained at over 98%, virtually eliminating any security gaps. Overall, having everything tracked in Freshservice means no more forgotten steps, fewer support escalations, and consistently high satisfaction from both end users and IT stakeholders.

Since adopting Freshservice, our business teams have seen a marked improvement in both speed and consistency of service delivery. Automating ticket routing and approval processes has cut our average first-response time from 4 hours to under 45 minutes (an 80% reduction). By enforcing SLAs and using built-in dashboards, we’ve achieved over 95% SLA compliance, compared to around 70% before.

Internally, teams spend far less time on manual status updates or chasing down approvals. Routine requests—like access changes, hardware provisioning, or software installations—now follow a standardized workflow, which has driven our overall ticket resolution time down by 50%. We’ve also seen a noticeable bump in employee satisfaction scores (up 20% on our internal survey) because requests are fulfilled more predictably and transparently.

Having all these processes centralized in Freshservice means fewer miscommunications, fewer dropped tasks, and a clearer view for managers to identify bottlenecks. As a result, we’ve been able to reallocate roughly 25% of our support team’s effort toward proactive projects instead of firefighting daily tickets.

column15: Our current workflows for onboarding and offboarding via FS can definitely be improved today. The round robin ticket assignment is not accurate and tickets get stuck in limbo. If you have a parent plus child tickets, the DTS techs have to wait to close the main ticket until all the child tickets have been closed by other IT teams. The offboarding tickets act the same as far as closure. Offboarding has a hardware equipment ticket for ITAM to retrieve assets but then there is a main term ticket that gets stuck with our DTS team until all has been completed for them to close out. They hold onto this ticket even though they do not work anything. Not all hiring managers have access to view the ticket notes due to license restrictions...so DTS has to communicate to the hiring manager when all the notes are within the tickets.
